newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end lower ahead of options expiry.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end lower ahead of options expiry.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday in very thin trading as options speculators exploited the low volume to move prices, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.49 percent, or 1.19 points, to 242.74 on very low all-share turnover of 70 million shekels against 80 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.65 percent lower at 250.84.

"Trading was very dull today and Maof options speculators used the opportunity to push the index towards 250 ahead of the March contract expiration on Thursday," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.

"The market was extremely quiet today. All investors are waiting to see what will happen with the peace talks," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Leahva Securities. "Nobody wants to make any move before there is more information, despite the fact that share prices are very attractive."

U.S. President Bill Clinton has ordered his chief Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross back to the region to try and salvage Israeli-PLO talks threatened by recent unrest. Ross was due to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Morocco on Thursday.
"Trading was trendless and investors are waiting for political developments to make a decision. Foreign investors are also sitting on the fence. The market is simply dead," Weiss said.

Koor Industries fell 0.75 percent to 29,289 agorot. Koor said on Wednesday that 1996 fourth-quarter earnings per American depositary receipt (ADR) were unchanged at 1.06 shekels. Net income was up 2.8 percent to 78 million shekel.
Supersol closed down 1.5 percent to 965 agorot. Lehman Brothers said on Wednesday that the company was cut to "outperform" from "buy".

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which fell 0.5 percent to 539 agorot on volume of 3.1 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 0.5 percent to 655 agorot on turnover of 3.0 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.5 percent to 18,995 agorot on volume of 2.5 million shekels.
